description:
Coordinator & Front-of-House Ambassador for a Luxury Clinic

Job Overview
- Role: Clinic Coordinator & Front-of-House Ambassador.
- Pay Rate: Up to £16 per hour (dependent on experience).
- Part time: 20-30 hrs per week - Thursday, Friday and 2 Saturdays per month.
- Location: Clinic (On-site)

As the first point of contact, you will deliver a 5-star, luxury front-of-house experience for our clients. You will manage the daily flow of the clinic, optimise practitioners' schedules, oversee inventory, actively drive clinic growth through patient retention strategies, social media support, and local marketing initiatives, while providing direct administrative support to ensure seamless daily operations.

Key Responsibilities and Duties

1. Front of House & Patient Experience
- Provide a pristine, warm, and professional welcome to all patients arriving at the clinic, including offering refreshments.
- Manage patient check-ins, guide them through necessary medical history paperwork, and coordinate waiting room flow.
- Serve as the brand ambassador, ensuring the reception and waiting areas are flawlessly presented at all times.
- Handle all incoming phone calls, emails, and digital inquiries promptly, converting inquiries into bookings and managing patient deposits

2. Commercial & Growth Support
- Social Media & Content: Capture high-quality, authorised photo and video content during clinic downtime to support marketing channels.
- Local Marketing: Assist with community networking and local business outreach.
- Event Coordination: Support the planning and execution of in-clinic events such as VIP evenings, product launches, or promotional open days by managing RSVPs and guest relations.

3. Clinic Preparation & Stock Control
- Clinic Room Prep: Arrive ahead of clinic hours to tidy, reset, and prepare treatment rooms, ensuring they are pristine and set up according to practitioner preferences.
- Stock Auditing: Perform regular inventory checks on clinical consumables and retail skincare lines to prevent shortages.
- Merchandising: Ensure front-of-house retail displays are fully stocked, meticulously clean, and visually appealing.

4. Clinic Efficiency & Compliance
- Proactively manage the digital booking.
- Maintain strict patient confidentiality and data compliance in line with GDPR regulations.
- Process payments securely and handle billing queries.

Candidate Requirements

Essential:
- Experience: Minimum 2 years of experience in a premium reception, administrative, or customer-facing role (e.g., private medical, aesthetic clinic, luxury spa).
- Communication: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills with a polished, professional telephone manner and a confident approach to client outreach.
- Tech-Savvy: Highly proficient in digital tools, Microsoft Office, and electronic booking software. Comfortable using smartphones and apps for social media content capture.
- Attributes: High attention to detail, strong organisational skills, commercial awareness, and a genuine interest in the aesthetics and skincare industry.

Desirable:
- 2-3 years of experience in a premium reception, administrative, or customer-facing role in a private medical or an aesthetic clinic.
- Prior experience handling medical records or working in a regulated clinical setting.
- Basic understanding of social media platforms (Instagram/TikTok) for business.

Benefits
- Competitive salary of up to £16 per hour (depending on experience).
- Private Health Insurance.
- Generous discounts on treatments and skincare products.

A leading and reputable charity based in Belfast, are currently seeking a Hub Coordinator to join their team.

Job Purpose:

You will be responsible for acting as a first point of contact for all Services across a geographical area from the local coordination Hub. You will lead and support the referral process, co-ordination and booking of care as required, ensuring data and information is accurately inputted into operational and clinical systems. You will work alongside the Senior Co-ordinators in order to ensure the smooth running of the co-ordination hub and will also work alongside and liaise with clinical support & management staff as well as, customers.

Essential Criteria:
- Previous experience within a similar role and of working within a customer service environment.
- IT proficient with the knowledge and use of Microsoft Office Word, Excel, Email and Internet.
- Experience of producing management and statistical reports.
- Excellent communication skills both written and verbal - with the ability to communicate with stakeholders at all levels.
- Ability to manage and prioritise a busy workload.

- Maintenance of the daily rota which supports the allocation of staff. This includes responsibility for monitoring and highlighting the utilisation of each service to higher staff and management.
- Confirming changes to rotas directly with staff and managing these changes on the systems.
- Direct liaison/negotiation with staff regarding their ability to cover shifts when they are not on the formal rota.
- Using the Robotic Process Automation system to add referrals into eCommunity and EMIS/SystmOne.
- Input of new customer details to systems ensuring that all key information is accurate and available to the staff.
- Updating information on systems provided by staff as required.
- Communication with customers regarding care provision via telephone. Liaising with referrers to check care packages are in place prior to offering those into care.
- Being responsible for identifying and highlighting rapid discharge and emergency referrals to the Hub Manager & staff.
- Responsibility for ensuring that all the above is clearly documented on Systems so there is no doubt or confusion relating to the status of the care and that all notes are of a high standard to support potential audits.
- Supporting the management of a prioritised caseloads for all services with clinical colleagues.
- Undertaking general administration of the electronic systems, to ensure that accurate records are maintained.
- Coordination of clinical service based on priority and handovers.
- Following discussion with the Senior Coordinator/ Hub Manager allocation of staff to patients.
- Prioritisation to ensure continuity of care and efficient deployment of available staff in line with procedures, standards and processes.
- Calculating the shift and travel time to ensure that staff have minimal down time and optimum numbers of patients receive care.
- Communication regarding confirmation of visits booked.
- Communication with referrers regarding confirmation of visits booked.

title: Front of House Administrator
description:
Honeycomb is delighted to be working with a large public sector organisation to recruit a temporary Front of House Administrator. Based in Carrickfergus, this is an excellent opportunity to join a well-established organisation on an initial 3-month temporary contract.

The Company

This is an exciting opportunity to join a well-established public sector organisation, offering full-time hours and the chance to gain valuable experience within a professional customer-focused environment.

The Role

As a Front of House Administrator, you will act as the first point of contact for visitors and customers, providing a friendly and professional service. You will handle enquiries, manage reception and work across a number of departments, while supporting customer payments, cash handling and the accurate maintenance of financial records.

Key Responsibilities
- Respond to customer enquiries in person and by telephone, providing advice and directing queries to the appropriate department.
- Manage the day-to-day operation of the reception area, including visitor sign-in, passes and general reception duties.
- Process customer payments accurately across face-to-face, telephone and online channels.
- Handle, record and reconcile cash, cheques and other income in line with financial procedures.
- Maintain accurate customer, financial and administrative records using computerised systems.
- Process incoming and outgoing post, deliveries and courier items securely and efficiently.

The Person

The successful candidate will have a strong background in customer service and administration, with excellent communication and organisational skills. You will be available for an immediate start and meet the following essential criteria:

Essential Criteria
- 5 GCSEs, including English Language and Maths (Grade C or above), or equivalent qualifications.
- A minimum of 2 years' experience working within a customer service environment, including dealing effectively with the public.
- Strong IT skills and experience using computerised systems.
- Previous cash-handling experience, including the use of credit/debit card machines.
- Alternatively, if you do not have 5 GCSEs, you should demonstrate 4 years' relevant experience in the required areas, including suitable English and Maths qualifications.

Package & Benefits
- Immediate start available
- £14.13 per hour
- 37 hours per week
- Monday to Friday
- 3-month temporary contract
- Opportunity to gain valuable experience within a well-established public sector organisation
